probes.question: In the Caesar cipher as described for Julius Caesar, which letter does A become when encrypting?
True or false: ROT13 is a Caesar shift of thirteen.

image.alt: Many paper Caesar cipher wheels with two rings of alphabet letters, lying on a round tray

body.claim: The Roman historian Suetonius writes that Julius Caesar used a cipher with a shift of three (A becoming D when encrypting) to protect messages of military significance.
body.why: A Caesar shift of thirteen is also performed in the ROT13 cipher, a simple method of obfuscating text found on Usenet and used to obscure text such as joke punchlines and story spoilers.
